_about: Identity cards for prompts. The character sheet image is always the authority; these short descriptions only help the image model match each sheet to a name. Descriptions were written after inspecting the sheets in Charactors/CHANDRUSH CHARACTERS and the approved Opening V04 art (2026-10-11). Leave out sheet lettering (T-shirt slogan, sketchbook cover words) - story art shows them plain.

Ahana.card: Ahana (curly dark hair, teal jacket over a coral T-shirt, charcoal cargo trousers, navy backpack)
Ahana.props: small spiral sketchbook (plain cover in story art); navy backpack with a compass charm
Ahana.watch: Big voluminous curls; warm brown skin; white-and-blue sneakers. No slogan text on the T-shirt in story art.

Vihaan.card: Vihaan (thick tousled black hair, mustard-yellow jacket, navy T-shirt, slate-blue cargo trousers, deep-red backpack)
Vihaan.watch: Mustard jacket and red backpack are his strongest recognition cues.

Navya.card: Navya (two long dark braids, maroon jacket over a navy-and-white striped top, denim cargo jeans, tan crossbody pouch)
Navya.props: tan leather crossbody satchel - the manuscript calls it her pouch / tool pouch; black wristwatch
Navya.watch: Twin braids with a centre parting and short fringe. The literal filename NAYA INVITATION DISCOVERY.png refers to Navya.

Tez.card: Tez (a small tiger cub with a navy neckerchief and a round silver button)
Tez.props: navy neckerchief with silver trim and a round silver button
Tez.watch: The sheet shows black stripes. From V07 p7 the story paints his stripes BLUE (approved Opening art) and the manuscript names faded pale-grey stripes per scene - copy each panel's 'Scene-specific stripe colours' sentence into its prompt.

Tara.card: Tara (an elderly woman with a long silver braid, deep-indigo robe with gold motifs, peacock-teal sash and a tall bronze staff)
Tara.props: tall bronze staff with its ornamental finial exactly as on the sheet; cream kurta and trousers; navy juttis
Tara.watch: Dignified, realistic elder. Manuscript panels usually put the staff in her own LEFT hand - always state the hand.
